Definition: Spirit, breath and wind — the life-giving presence and power of God, and the breath that animates every living creature.
BiblicalUsage: Ruach hovers over creation, breathes life into Adam, fills prophets and craftsmen, and in Ezekiel raises dry bones to life. Its range — wind, breath, Spirit — shows one powerful, personal presence at work.
TheologicalSignificance: Ruach is hope for the lifeless places: the same Spirit who raised dry bones in Ezekiel and raised Jesus from the dead lives in believers, renewing what seemed beyond repair.
